entries.symptom: An automated change is applied to an unknown repository state.
entries.rootCause: Baseline identity was not treated as an invariant.
entries.correctiveAction: Require exact HEAD, expected branch, clean status and expected file identities before mutation.
entries.permanentGuard: Every transactional pack validates its immutable baseline before the first effect.

entries.symptom: Normal native stderr is interpreted as a PowerShell failure.
entries.rootCause: Windows PowerShell 5.1 can surface native stderr as NativeCommandError under ErrorActionPreference=Stop.
entries.correctiveAction: Use a native-command wrapper and judge native success from process exit code.
entries.permanentGuard: Native stderr alone is never proof of failure.

entries.symptom: A generated NextGen clone is rediscovered as a competing source repository.
entries.rootCause: All clones sharing the same remote were treated as equally authoritative.
entries.correctiveAction: Prefer the canonical reference clone and exclude generated workspaces from fallback discovery.
entries.permanentGuard: Generated workspaces never silently become source baselines.

entries.symptom: Successive patch-on-patch revisions make provenance uncertain.
entries.rootCause: A failed infrastructure artifact was repaired incrementally instead of rebuilt from its contract.
entries.correctiveAction: Rebuild from the latest immutable validated baseline.
entries.permanentGuard: Published/released pack revisions are immutable; infrastructure defects trigger reconstruction.

entries.symptom: An automated run waits for unexpected user input.
entries.rootCause: Interactive commands or authentication prompts were allowed inside automation.
entries.correctiveAction: Use non-interactive modes and fail explicitly when required data are unavailable.
entries.permanentGuard: Read-Host, Pause and interactive prompt flows are forbidden in automated paths.

entries.symptom: A feature exists in one layer but is absent or only nominally represented in another.
entries.rootCause: Feature completion was assessed locally instead of across the scientific software chain.
entries.correctiveAction: Track every extension through the universal extension contract and scientific coverage registry.
entries.permanentGuard: No feature is declared fully supported until all applicable layers are explicitly in parity.

entries.symptom: StrictMode raises PropertyNotFoundException when .Count is read from a scalar returned by a function that normally represents a collection.
entries.rootCause: Windows PowerShell unwraps zero/one-element pipeline results unless the caller explicitly materializes an array.
entries.correctiveAction: Materialize collection-valued function results with @(...), and use @($value).Count in guards.
entries.permanentGuard: Infrastructure code must never assume pipeline collection cardinality from the runtime type of an unmaterialized result.

entries.symptom: A directory containing several new files appears as one '?? directory/' entry and fails exact expected-path comparison.
entries.rootCause: git status --porcelain uses normal untracked-file collapsing unless --untracked-files=all is requested.
entries.correctiveAction: All exact-scope calculations use git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all.
entries.permanentGuard: Any packaging/preflight engine comparing expected paths to Git status must request untracked-files=all and validate individual files, never directory summaries.

entries.symptom: A prerelease declared in version.json is not fully reflected when the candidate is built from an uncommitted version change.
entries.rootCause: Nerdbank.GitVersioning derives some version semantics from committed Git history; its documentation explicitly warns that some version.json changes are not effective until committed.
entries.correctiveAction: Create the candidate commit inside the disposable shadow worktree before running Build-Validated.
entries.permanentGuard: Version-changing candidates are validated only from a clean committed shadow candidate.

entries.symptom: BuildVersionSimple omits the prerelease suffix and can make prerelease artifacts appear stable.
entries.rootCause: BuildVersionSimple is a numeric simple version and is not the public human prerelease identity.
entries.correctiveAction: Expose PrereleaseVersion and compute a DisplayVersion equal to the declared version.json semantic version.
entries.permanentGuard: Artifact names, documentation display and validated-build summaries use DisplayVersion; a version-identity validator enforces declared/version-tool parity.

entries.symptom: A shadow working-tree replay validates source bytes but not the exact Git commit identity later used by versioning.
entries.rootCause: The previous pipeline built an uncommitted shadow then replayed files into the real branch.
entries.correctiveAction: Commit the candidate in the shadow, validate that exact commit, then fast-forward the real branch to the same validated commit object.
entries.permanentGuard: For versioned candidates, shadow commit SHA and final local branch HEAD must be identical.

entries.symptom: A legacy script succeeds normally but fails when invoked from a StrictMode-enabled caller because an unmaterialized pipeline result is treated as a scalar.
entries.rootCause: StrictMode exposes collection-cardinality assumptions in nested infrastructure scripts.
entries.correctiveAction: Make Test-VersioningPreflight strict-safe itself: enable StrictMode locally, materialize nested version search results, and wrap Count guards.
entries.permanentGuard: Critical preflight scripts must pass when StrictMode is enabled in their own scope, not merely when called from permissive callers.

entries.symptom: A safety scanner flags the forbidden pattern inside its own transformation literal instead of active code.
entries.rootCause: The static guard did not distinguish executable source from quoted OldText fixtures.
entries.correctiveAction: Scope safety checks to active statements or AST nodes and explicitly exclude transformation literals/fixtures.
entries.permanentGuard: Preflight detectors must include positive and negative fixtures and must not self-match on their own test strings.

entries.symptom: A multi-line text anchor fails because line endings or formatting differ despite the baseline file being semantically the expected one.
entries.rootCause: Critical infrastructure reconstruction depended on exact multi-line textual formatting.
entries.correctiveAction: For critical files with an exact known baseline blob, verify the blob SHA and replace the complete file with a canonical payload.
entries.permanentGuard: Versioning/preflight critical files are reconstructed as complete canonical files after exact baseline blob verification; multi-line textual anchors are forbidden there.

entries.symptom: A failed candidate can leave a temporary branch even when no candidate commit was created.
entries.rootCause: Cleanup was conditional only on a non-null candidate commit.
entries.correctiveAction: If no candidate commit was created, delete the temporary branch only when it is proven to still point to the immutable baseline. Retain committed candidates for recovery.
entries.permanentGuard: Temporary branch cleanup is state-aware: baseline-only branches are disposable; committed validated candidates are retained until successful finalization.

entries.symptom: A versioning gate fails with MSB4057 because the NBGV GetBuildVersion target is unavailable in a fresh shadow worktree.
entries.rootCause: The gate called Get-LotSizingVersion.ps1 with -SkipRestore before any project restore had materialized NuGet/MSBuild imports in the new worktree.
entries.correctiveAction: Pre-build version identity validation performs its own restore. -SkipRestore is allowed only after an explicit successful restore in the same worktree.
entries.permanentGuard: Any version probe executed before the build restore must not use -SkipRestore; build ordering and restore assumptions are part of the validation contract.

entries.symptom: Semantic instance validation duplicates structural/referential validation rules already owned by Core.
entries.rootCause: Validation responsibilities are not separated by layer.
entries.correctiveAction: InstanceModelChecker composes SupplyChainValidator diagnostics and adds only instance-level semantic rules.
entries.permanentGuard: Structural/referential truth remains owned by Core.SupplyChainValidator; InstanceModelChecker must not independently reimplement those rules.

entries.symptom: Replacing the flat historical feature vector in one step risks XML/API breakage and loss of classification semantics.
entries.rootCause: LotSizingProblemFeatures mixes many scientific domains in one historical vector.
entries.correctiveAction: Introduce typed descriptors first as a lossless non-serialized bridge, prove full round-trip equivalence, then migrate extraction toward Core -> Descriptor -> Features.
entries.permanentGuard: Every represented primary feature must remain losslessly mappable until formally deprecated under an explicit compatibility policy.

entries.symptom: A compact transactional launcher fails before shadow creation with PositionalParameterNotFound for System.Object[].
entries.rootCause: Condensed PowerShell helper functions and positional calls passed array-valued native arguments through ambiguous positional binding under Windows PowerShell 5.1.
entries.correctiveAction: Use explicit helper functions with named parameters for executable, repository path and string-array arguments.
entries.permanentGuard: Transactional pack engines must not use compact positional wrappers for array-valued arguments; validated explicit wrappers are the canonical implementation.

entries.symptom: BOM dependencies and physical supply-flow arcs are conflated into one topology.
entries.rootCause: Product structure and logistics topology are both directed graphs but have different semantics and cycle rules.
entries.correctiveAction: Maintain separate ProductStructureDescriptor and SupplyNetworkDescriptor analyses; BOM cycles remain invalid while physical supply cycles are represented by HasCycles.
entries.permanentGuard: No physical-network classifier or notation token may derive topology from ComponentRequirements, and no BOM validator may reject a transport-flow cycle solely because it is cyclic.

entries.symptom: Temporal pattern classification becomes non-deterministic near numerical tolerance boundaries or silently mixes historical and universal notations.
entries.rootCause: Zero, constant and monotone classes overlap mathematically, and floating-point tolerance can make both monotone directions appear true.
entries.correctiveAction: Use an explicit global-scale tolerance and canonical specificity Zero > Constant > one-direction monotonicity > General; tolerance-induced bidirectional ambiguity falls back to General.
entries.permanentGuard: Historical Bitran-Yanasse alpha/beta/gamma/delta codes remain slash-separated and isolated from the universal alpha|beta|gamma notation.

entries.symptom: A notation string becomes ambiguous, order-dependent, or impossible to evolve compatibly.
entries.rootCause: Human-readable tokens are treated as free text instead of a versioned grammar backed by a typed AST and canonical renderer.
entries.correctiveAction: Use a versioned LSDM scheme, typed alpha/beta/gamma AST, stable token catalog, strict parser and deterministic canonical renderer.
entries.permanentGuard: Generated notation must satisfy Render(Parse(Render(Generate(descriptor)))) == Render(Generate(descriptor)); historical alias notations remain separate projections.

entries.symptom: A partial notation is treated as a closed-world description, so omitted optional characteristics become false contradictions.
entries.rootCause: Generation notation and problem-specification semantics are conflated.
entries.correctiveAction: Exact matching uses full canonical generated equality; compatibility matching interprets explicitly present tokens as positive requirements and omitted optional beta/network modifiers as unconstrained.
entries.permanentGuard: Matcher precedence is Contradiction > Incomplete > Exact > Compatible, and Exact always requires canonical equality with generated notation.

entries.symptom: DRP or MRP is described as a lot-sizing model/problem class, or a physical network topology is named after a planning paradigm.
entries.rootCause: Structural properties, planning paradigms, problem classes, formulations and solution methods are mixed in one classification vocabulary.
entries.correctiveAction: Introduce explicit ScientificConceptCategory dimensions and replace DRP-named topology inference with neutral observable network properties.
entries.permanentGuard: DRP and MRP are categorized only as PlanningParadigm; physical topology descriptors must remain paradigm-neutral; mappings may relate concepts but never collapse their categories.

entries.symptom: A pack fails the staged-path scope check because expectedPaths contains a payload file whose content is identical to the immutable baseline.
entries.rootCause: The pack declared intended payload files rather than the exact Git diff that the candidate commit can actually contain.
entries.correctiveAction: Compute expectedPaths from files that are provably changed relative to the exact baseline; omit byte-identical baseline files even if they were consulted or copied during pack fabrication.
entries.permanentGuard: Before sealing a pack, every expectedPaths entry must differ from the exact baseline or be a genuinely new path; every actual changed path must be listed, and baseline-identical files must be excluded.

entries.symptom: A historical classification is claimed to be fully represented by universal notation even though one or more historical dimensions have no equivalent token/attribute in the current grammar.
entries.rootCause: Historical mapping coverage is implicit rather than represented as data.
entries.correctiveAction: Historical mapping objects must report Exact or Partial coverage and preserve every unmapped historical dimension explicitly instead of silently dropping it.
entries.permanentGuard: A historical mapping may be marked Exact only when every source classification dimension is represented losslessly in the target universal specification.

entries.symptom: A historical mapping introduces special-purpose universal tokens that encode the name or position of one literature classification instead of reusable problem semantics.
entries.rootCause: Historical notation is used as the target grammar rather than mapped onto generic semantic concepts.
entries.correctiveAction: Represent temporal behavior through generic TP:<parameter>=<pattern> qualifiers and map historical schemes onto them.
entries.permanentGuard: Universal notation tokens must describe reusable lot-sizing semantics; historical names/positions remain in mapping layers and may not become canonical universal tokens.

entries.symptom: A historical mapping test expects the canonical notation of one temporal profile while constructing a different temporal-profile fixture.
entries.rootCause: The expected canonical string was copied from another test case and was not tied explicitly to the fixture's historical code.
entries.correctiveAction: Historical mapping tests must first assert the source historical code produced by their fixture, then assert the universal projection of that same profile.
entries.permanentGuard: No mapping test may reuse a canonical expected notation from another fixture without first asserting the exact source classification/profile represented by its own input.

entries.symptom: A literature classification token is mapped by acronym similarity instead of source semantics, e.g. Wolsey SC interpreted as setup cost or SL interpreted as lost sales.
entries.rootCause: Historical token labels collide with LotSizingDataModel canonical abbreviations.
entries.correctiveAction: Historical enums preserve source-token namespaces and mapping code uses source definitions, never string-name coincidence.
entries.permanentGuard: Every historical token mapping must be backed by an explicit semantic case; ambiguous or unsupported tokens remain unrepresented rather than being matched to a similarly named universal feature.

entries.symptom: Explicitly uncapacitated production is represented only by absence of a capacity token.
entries.rootCause: Positive-constraint matching interprets omission as unspecified, so absence cannot encode a required negative condition.
entries.correctiveAction: Derive ProductionCapacityRegime and encode explicit uncapacitated production with generic token Uncap:P.
entries.permanentGuard: Semantically meaningful absence/negative conditions require explicit representation whenever omission means unconstrained.

entries.symptom: A scientific property derived from detailed parameter series is either guessed from coarse booleans or encoded as a historical acronym in universal notation.
entries.rootCause: The notation had temporal derived analyses but no generic tri-state carrier for other derived mathematical conditions.
entries.correctiveAction: Represent reusable positive requirements as UniversalSemanticCondition and actual analyses as Unknown/Satisfied/NotSatisfied through UniversalDerivedSemantics.
entries.permanentGuard: Historical acronyms may map to generic conditions, but universal semantic conditions must have an explicit scientific analyzer or already-modeled derivation.

entries.symptom: A historical problem class remains wholly unrepresented even after one of its defining dimensions becomes generically expressible.
entries.rootCause: Historical mapping gaps are treated monolithically instead of dimension by dimension.
entries.correctiveAction: Close each representable source dimension independently while retaining every still-unrepresented dimension explicitly.
entries.permanentGuard: Historical coverage is Exact only when the gap list is empty; partial closure must remove only the source dimensions actually represented.

entries.symptom: A matcher test expects Exact while its specification intentionally omits a known canonical descriptor characteristic.
entries.rootCause: The test confuses 'all explicit requirements are satisfied' with canonical equality of the complete generated notation.
entries.correctiveAction: Tests for Exact must include every characteristic emitted by Generate(descriptor, derivedSemantics); tests with omitted satisfied characteristics must assert Compatible.
entries.permanentGuard: Matcher tests must separately prove Exact for canonical equality and Compatible for positive partial specifications, even when all explicit semantic-condition requirements are satisfied.

entries.symptom: An acronym such as CLSP, ULSP or MLLS is silently resolved to one canonical class even though literature usage is cardinality/capacity ambiguous.
entries.rootCause: Aliases are treated as unique identifiers rather than many-to-many literature labels.
entries.correctiveAction: Use a resolver returning Unknown/Unique/Ambiguous and canonical LSDM class codes that explicitly encode item cardinality/capacity where needed.
entries.permanentGuard: Ambiguous aliases must never be auto-resolved to the first catalog entry.

entries.symptom: A scientifically known problem class receives an executable universal specification before its actual decision semantics exist in the model.
entries.rootCause: Scientific inventory and implementation support are conflated.
entries.correctiveAction: Separate Executable from CatalogOnly problem-class support; catalog-only classes carry explicit capability gaps and no universal core specification.
entries.permanentGuard: A class can become Executable only after all defining semantics required for membership are represented and testable.

entries.symptom: An instance with backlogging, safety stock, lead time or another industrial extension is rejected from its underlying lot-sizing core class.
entries.rootCause: Problem-class membership is treated as closed-world equality rather than core-plus-extension classification.
entries.correctiveAction: Distinguish ExactCore from CompatibleExtension and enumerate modeled extensions separately.
entries.permanentGuard: Canonical class assessment uses positive core specifications; supported extra features must be reported as extensions rather than false contradictions.

entries.symptom: Detected notation overwrites, reuses or silently trusts notation declared by a source instance or publication.
entries.rootCause: Source claims and computed scientific evidence are stored as one field.
entries.correctiveAction: Keep DeclaredNotation and DetectedNotation as separate objects and compare them explicitly through the universal matcher.
entries.permanentGuard: Detected notation must always be generated from descriptors/analyses; a declaration may only be parsed and compared, never used as detected evidence.

entries.symptom: Detecting a problem class implicitly assigns a planning paradigm, mathematical formulation or solution method.
entries.rootCause: Orthogonal scientific taxonomy axes are collapsed in one classifier.
entries.correctiveAction: ScientificClassificationCoverage declares which axes are analyzed, capability-only or not inferred.
entries.permanentGuard: Problem-class detection may not infer MRP/DRP, formulations or solving methods unless a dedicated axis analyzer is explicitly implemented.

entries.symptom: Scientific classification runs on an instance with blocking structural/model diagnostics.
entries.rootCause: Classification bypasses InstanceModelChecker.
entries.correctiveAction: LotSizingInstance analysis composes InstanceModelChecker and honors CanClassify before extracting scientific classification.
entries.permanentGuard: Blocking instance validation must produce LSDM-SCI-001 and no detected notation/problem-class claim.

entries.symptom: The existence of a historical-to-universal mapper is reported as automatic detection of the complete historical source code.
entries.rootCause: Mapping capability and inverse historical classification are conflated.
entries.correctiveAction: HistoricalClassificationCapability reports mapping and complete-code detection independently.
entries.permanentGuard: CanMapDeclaredClassification never implies CanDetectCompleteHistoricalCode.

entries.symptom: A formulation is considered scientifically supported solely because CanBuild(instance) returns true.
entries.rootCause: Technical build preconditions are conflated with semantic/modeling coverage.
entries.correctiveAction: Add explicit mathematical-formulation scientific profiles and require verified canonical-class/extension coverage separately from CanBuild.
entries.permanentGuard: Automatic scientific selection requires ScientificCompatible; concrete instance selection additionally requires CanBuild(instance).

entries.symptom: An unprofiled or unverified formulation capability is silently treated as supported.
entries.rootCause: Capability absence is interpreted optimistically.
entries.correctiveAction: Use Undetermined for unprofiled formulations and unverified extensions.
entries.permanentGuard: Undetermined formulations/extensions are never auto-selected.

entries.symptom: A scientific formulation profile claims support that has no corresponding registered variable/objective/constraint implementation evidence.
entries.rootCause: Capability metadata drifts from the actual formulation factory.
entries.correctiveAction: Ground profile support in concrete builder families and keep evidence with the profile.
entries.permanentGuard: Changes to standard formulation builder families require scientific capability-profile review and tests.

entries.symptom: A stored solution cannot identify the canonical problem class and scientific formulation context under which it was generated.
entries.rootCause: Generation metadata records algorithm/solver execution but not scientific classification/formulation evidence.
entries.correctiveAction: Persist dependency-neutral scientific provenance through reserved solution-generation parameters.
entries.permanentGuard: Solver provenance capture requires detected classification and successful scientifically compatible formulation selection.

entries.symptom: Scientific provenance creates a Solution->Instance/Solver dependency or a mandatory XML schema break.
entries.rootCause: Cross-layer provenance is represented by direct domain-object references.
entries.correctiveAction: Store neutral string snapshot fields in the existing optional Parameters collection.
entries.permanentGuard: Solution remains independent from Instance/Solver and existing solution XML stays readable.

entries.symptom: Scientific provenance state is confused with mathematical feasibility.
entries.rootCause: Traceability evidence and constraint/objective evidence are collapsed.
entries.correctiveAction: Keep scientific provenance checking orthogonal to the numerical SolutionChecker.
entries.permanentGuard: Provenance states never substitute for feasibility/objective/constraint verification.

entries.symptom: A newer classifier detecting additional compatible semantics makes older provenance appear contradictory.
entries.rootCause: Recorded notation is compared by raw string equality.
entries.correctiveAction: Revalidate recorded notation as a positive universal specification; Compatible becomes Stale.
entries.permanentGuard: Raw notation-string inequality alone cannot establish provenance contradiction.

entries.symptom: Scientific preflight selects one formulation but the delegated technical SolverRequest remains automatic or names another formulation.
entries.rootCause: Scientific selection is advisory rather than constraining the actual technical solve request.
entries.correctiveAction: Create a separate delegated SolverRequest whose FormulationName is pinned to the scientifically selected formulation ID.
entries.permanentGuard: ScientificSelectedFormulationId must equal DelegatedSolverRequest.FormulationName before solver execution.

entries.symptom: Scientific provenance is written before a normalized LotSizingSolution exists or after a solve that produced no solution.
entries.rootCause: Provenance capture is tied to solve invocation rather than successful solution mapping.
entries.correctiveAction: Capture provenance only after SolverRunResult.HasSolution is true and formulation identity has been verified.
entries.permanentGuard: No normalized solution means no scientific solution provenance.

entries.symptom: Scientific preflight, solver execution, numerical feasibility and provenance verification are collapsed into one boolean success flag.
entries.rootCause: Independent evidence channels are not retained in the orchestration result.
entries.correctiveAction: ScientificSolvePipelineResult stores classification, formulation selection, SolverRunResult, numerical verification and provenance verification separately.
entries.permanentGuard: End-to-end coherence is derived from requested channels; no channel substitutes for another.

entries.symptom: A solution is attributed to the scientifically selected formulation although SolverRunResult reports a different formulation.
entries.rootCause: Actual formulation identity is not rechecked after technical solver execution.
entries.correctiveAction: Compare SolverRunResult.FormulationName with scientific selection before provenance capture.
entries.permanentGuard: Formulation drift is blocking for provenance capture and returns LSDM-PIPE-011.

entries.symptom: CPLEX/Gurobi/Xpress/CBC are classified as solution methods instead of native solver backends.
entries.rootCause: Algorithmic method and implementation backend are collapsed into one resolution label.
entries.correctiveAction: Separate ScientificSolutionMethodDefinition from ScientificSolverBackendDefinition.
entries.permanentGuard: SolverKind values may never be used as scientific solution-method identifiers.

entries.symptom: A literature method family is auto-selected although no executable adapter exists in LotSizingDataModel.
entries.rootCause: Scientific relevance is conflated with implementation availability.
entries.correctiveAction: Solution methods have Executable or CatalogOnly support levels; automatic planning selects only ExecutableCompatible candidates.
entries.permanentGuard: CatalogOnly methods are never auto-selected.

entries.symptom: Scientific solution provenance records problem/formulation but cannot state the algorithmic method family or actual backend.
entries.rootCause: Provenance schema v1 ended at formulation compatibility.
entries.correctiveAction: Schema v2 records solutionMethodId, solutionMethodCategory and solverBackendKind while retaining v1 read compatibility.
entries.permanentGuard: New end-to-end pipeline solutions use provenance schema v2.

entries.symptom: A requested or scientifically compatible backend family differs from the backend actually reported by SolverRunResult.
entries.rootCause: Only formulation identity is rechecked after solve.
entries.correctiveAction: Validate SolverRunResult.SolverKind against the scientific resolution plan before provenance capture.
entries.permanentGuard: Backend drift blocks schema-v2 provenance capture and emits LSDM-PIPE-012/013.

entries.symptom: A transversal helper signature gains a required argument but one or more existing call sites are left with the previous arity/order, producing a compile-time CS7036 failure.
entries.rootCause: The change is propagated by broad textual replacement without a complete call-site parity audit after the helper contract changes.
entries.correctiveAction: After changing an internal helper signature, enumerate every call site and verify that every invocation carries the new argument in the intended semantic position.
entries.permanentGuard: Pack fabrication must statically audit all ScientificLotSizingSolvePipeline.Result(...) call sites against the helper contract before delivery; Build-Validated remains the final committed-candidate compiler gate.

entries.symptom: Start-up time/cost is represented with ordinary setup time/cost because the terms look similar.
entries.rootCause: Resource setup activation and the transition that starts a sequence of setups are conflated.
entries.correctiveAction: Use dedicated StartUpCost/StartUpTime Core parameters and distinct universal tokens SU/SUT.
entries.permanentGuard: Wolsey ST maps to universal SUT, never universal ST; start-up parameters remain separate from setup parameters in Core and descriptors.

entries.symptom: Wolsey SL is mapped to LostSales or to the mere presence of SellingPrice.
entries.rootCause: Additional optional sales above mandatory demand are confused with unmet demand or delivery revenue.
entries.correctiveAction: Keep VAR.SL:AdditionalSales as an explicit mapping gap until a separate additional-sales quantity/upper-bound decision exists.
entries.permanentGuard: SellingPrice alone cannot close Wolsey SL.

entries.symptom: A fixed initial-inventory input value is used to claim support for Wolsey DLSI's variable initial stock decision.
entries.rootCause: Input data and optimization decision variables are conflated.
entries.correctiveAction: Keep DLSI/DLS initial-stock gaps open until a real initial-stock decision semantic exists where scientifically appropriate.
entries.permanentGuard: HasInitialInventory never implies VariableInitialStockDecision.

entries.symptom: Pack fabrication injects a required parameter into the first textually matching param(...) block instead of the intended function, causing duplicate formal parameters in one function and a missing formal parameter in another.
entries.rootCause: A broad textual replacement targets a generic parameter-list shape rather than a named function contract.
entries.correctiveAction: Parameter-list edits in pack automation must target the exact named function block and the final script must be audited for duplicate formal parameters across every function.
entries.permanentGuard: Before delivery, enumerate every function param(...) block, reject duplicate formal parameter names case-insensitively, and explicitly assert the intended formal parameter set for transformed functions such as Apply-LsdmPayload and Assert-LsdmBaseline.

entries.symptom: A represented maximum lot size equal to zero is skipped as structural zero.
entries.rootCause: Minimum-bound filtering is incorrectly reused for upper bounds.
entries.correctiveAction: Always emit x<=Qmax for represented MaximumLotSize, including Qmax=0.
entries.permanentGuard: Null means absent; zero maximum means production forbidden.

entries.symptom: Relation-specific procurement capacity is described as supplier-wide shared capacity.
entries.rootCause: Physical resource scope is left implicit.
entries.correctiveAction: Define alpha.22 CapacityConstraint on SupplierDelivery as supplier-item-destination capacity.
entries.permanentGuard: Aggregate shared supplier capacity requires its own future semantic and formulation family.

entries.symptom: A new linear formulation constraint is reimplemented separately in SolutionChecker.
entries.rootCause: Feasibility equations are duplicated between formulation and checker.
entries.correctiveAction: Reuse MathematicalFeasibilityChecker over the generated model whenever business decisions already project to the constrained mathematical variables.
entries.permanentGuard: Do not duplicate maximum-lot or supplier-capacity equations in the checker.

entries.symptom: An extension moves from KnownUnsupported to supportedExtensions but legacy catalog tests still assert the old support state.
entries.rootCause: Capability metadata and its contract tests are edited independently.
entries.correctiveAction: Move each promoted extension in both the scientific profile and the support-state theory data in the same pack.
entries.permanentGuard: Pack fabrication audits that promoted extensions occur exactly once in the profile and in VerifiedSupported test data, and not in KnownUnsupported test data.

entries.symptom: The presence of a budget constraint changes gamma to Obj:Fin.
entries.rootCause: Financial feasibility constraints and the optimization criterion are conflated.
entries.correctiveAction: Keep financial constraints in beta (Fin) and determine gamma only from ObjectivePolicy.
entries.permanentGuard: HasFinancialConstraints never implies a Financial objective kind.

entries.symptom: A single total-cost objective with production, holding, transport and penalty terms is labeled multiobjective.
entries.rootCause: Objective components are confused with independent optimization criteria.
entries.correctiveAction: MultipleObjectives is detected only from an explicit ObjectivePolicy with multiple enabled criteria.
entries.permanentGuard: Several objective terms do not imply HasMultipleObjectives.

entries.symptom: A period expenditure cap is described as a full treasury/cash-flow model.
entries.rootCause: Payment timing, financing and cash balance mechanics are assumed without data.
entries.correctiveAction: Name and document the executable semantic PeriodicOperatingExpenditureBudget and exclude revenues/non-period terms by definition.
entries.permanentGuard: Do not claim cash-flow/trésorerie support until financing flows and payment timing exist explicitly.

entries.symptom: A formulation is considered compatible because all extensions are supported even though the requested objective family is unsupported.
entries.rootCause: Scientific formulation profiles check problem class/extensions but not objective kind.
entries.correctiveAction: Add SupportedObjectiveKinds and reject unsupported objective kinds with LSDM-FORM-013.
entries.permanentGuard: Scientific formulation compatibility requires both semantic extension coverage and objective-kind coverage.

entries.symptom: Financial budget constraints manually repeat all cost coefficients from objective builders.
entries.rootCause: Budget formulation duplicates economic objective construction.
entries.correctiveAction: Build period expenditure constraints from positive coefficients of the already assembled objective expression and canonical period domain keys.
entries.permanentGuard: PeriodicOperatingExpenditureBudgetConstraintFamilyBuilder reuses context.Model.Objective rather than maintaining a second cost catalog.

entries.symptom: A transaction aborts because a generic textual transform anchor is present more than once in the target file.
entries.rootCause: The transform identifies a local syntactic target with a globally generic statement instead of including the enclosing method/member identity in the anchor.
entries.correctiveAction: Scope transforms to the smallest uniquely identifiable structural region, such as the complete method signature/header plus the local insertion point.
entries.permanentGuard: A transform aimed at a known method/member must not use a generic body statement as its sole global anchor; fabrication audit must verify the structural target identity is embedded in the transform.

entries.symptom: Build-Validated rejects SCIENTIFIC-COVERAGE.json because a fabricated scientificStatus or implementationStatus value is outside the governance contract.
entries.rootCause: Pack fabrication treats governance status values as free text instead of validating them against the repository's accepted status vocabulary before candidate reconstruction.
entries.correctiveAction: Validate every scientific coverage status in the pack payload before creating a shadow worktree.
entries.permanentGuard: Accepted implementationStatus values are implemented, partial, unsupported. Accepted scientificStatus values are documented, implemented, planned, project-specific. Any other value aborts before worktree creation.

entries.symptom: New formulation code references a plausible but nonexistent modeling API symbol such as MathematicalObjectiveSense.
entries.rootCause: A new symbol name is inferred instead of verified against the existing modeling contract.
entries.correctiveAction: Before packaging, audit all newly referenced modeling enum/type names against existing source contracts; use ObjectiveSense for MathematicalObjective.Sense.
entries.permanentGuard: New formulation builders must pass a source-contract symbol audit for objective sense, constraint sense, domain keys and model context APIs before delivery.

entries.symptom: Presence of scheduling data automatically classifies or enables DLSP/CSLP/PLSP/GLSP.
entries.rootCause: Necessary scheduling facts are confused with the complete mathematical semantics of a named scheduling problem class.
entries.correctiveAction: Represent bucket/setup/changeover facts generically and keep named scheduling classes CatalogOnly until exact production and transition semantics are executable.
entries.permanentGuard: SchedulingProfile never by itself promotes DLSP/CSLP/PLSP/GLSP to Executable.

entries.symptom: GroupingConstraint is reused as MaximumSetupCount or as a bucket definition.
entries.rootCause: Different restrictions on setup events are conflated.
entries.correctiveAction: Keep GroupingConstraint as minimum setup spacing and introduce MaximumSetupCount separately.
entries.permanentGuard: GroupingConstraint semantics remain the sliding-window spacing invariant and are never reinterpreted by scheduling code.

entries.symptom: Sequence-dependent setup/changeover data are stored as an unordered item pair.
entries.rootCause: Directional setup-state transitions are treated as symmetric.
entries.correctiveAction: ProductionChangeover stores ordered FromItemId and ToItemId plus directional time/cost.
entries.permanentGuard: A->B and B->A are distinct scheduling definitions.

entries.symptom: Wolsey SB1/SB2/BB are mapped directly to newly added generic bucket tokens without a source-complete semantic proof.
entries.rootCause: The existence of a generic scheduling vocabulary is mistaken for evidence that a historical field is fully equivalent.
entries.correctiveAction: Close only SQT/SQC in alpha.24; retain machine bucket dimensions as explicit historical gaps.
entries.permanentGuard: Generic bucket support does not automatically close Wolsey Machines.Bucket.

entries.symptom: Standard MILP accepts scheduling extensions because Core and notation can represent them.
entries.rootCause: Representability is confused with formulation executability.
entries.correctiveAction: Register all alpha.24 scheduling extensions as KnownUnsupported in the standard formulation profile.
entries.permanentGuard: No scheduling extension becomes scientifically compatible until state/transition variables and constraints are implemented.

entries.symptom: A new test fixture instantiates a domain entity with a constructor signature that does not exist or omits a mandatory composition such as PlantWarehouse.
entries.rootCause: Fixture code is authored from an assumed convenience constructor instead of the actual domain constructor/cardinality contract.
entries.correctiveAction: Construct test entities with their real mandatory composed objects; for Plant use Plant(int, string, PlantWarehouse).
entries.permanentGuard: Before delivery, new domain-entity fixture constructors must be checked against the actual Core source contract. Scheduling fixtures must include an explicit PlantWarehouse when using the Plant parameterized constructor.

entries.symptom: A historical mapping gap is intentionally closed, but an older test still asserts that the same dimension must remain in UnrepresentedHistoricalDimensions.
entries.rootCause: The implementation and new positive tests are updated without auditing inherited negative-coverage tests for the same historical dimension.
entries.correctiveAction: When a historical dimension becomes representable, search the whole test suite for the old gap identifier and migrate stale negative assertions into positive mapping assertions while retaining unrelated gaps.
entries.permanentGuard: Pack fabrication must prove that each newly closed historical gap identifier is absent from inherited Assert.Contains gap assertions and that at least one positive semantic-feature assertion exists.

entries.symptom: A problem class becomes labeled Executable as soon as membership can be detected, even though no runnable formulation exists.
entries.rootCause: The problem-class support enum conflates scientific membership assessment with solver/formulation availability.
entries.correctiveAction: Introduce Classifiable support level and use it for DLSP/CSLP/PLSP until executable scheduling formulations exist.
entries.permanentGuard: Classifiable problem classes may be detected but cannot be treated as executable by formulation/method selection solely because membership is known.

entries.symptom: An integrated scheduling instance is simultaneously or primarily classified as generic MI-CLSP because its lot-sizing projection matches the generic core.
entries.rootCause: Problem-class detection ignores that scheduling semantics are strictly more specific than generic lot-sizing semantics.
entries.correctiveAction: When HasIntegratedScheduling is true, detect against classifiable scheduling classes only; do not silently fall back to generic six-core detection.
entries.permanentGuard: Integrated scheduling descriptors with insufficient scheduling semantics return no canonical member rather than degrade to generic CLSP.

entries.symptom: DLSP and CSLP are distinguished only by the SmallBucket flag.
entries.rootCause: The all-or-nothing versus continuous production-quantity rule is not represented.
entries.correctiveAction: Add SmallBucketProductionMode with AllOrNothing and Continuous semantics.
entries.permanentGuard: DLSP requires AllOrNothing; CSLP requires Continuous.

entries.symptom: PLSP is inferred from continuous small-bucket production without enforcing its one-transition/two-product structure.
entries.rootCause: Produced-item count and setup-transition count are omitted from canonical membership.
entries.correctiveAction: Represent MaximumProducedItemCount separately from MaximumSetupCount and require max produced items=2 plus at most one setup transition for PLSP.
entries.permanentGuard: PLSP classification requires both per-bucket item cardinality and setup-transition semantics.

entries.symptom: Single-machine canonical DLSP/CSLP/PLSP rules are applied to an instance with several scheduling resources without explicit multi-resource extension semantics.
entries.rootCause: Resource cardinality is ignored during canonical small-bucket membership assessment.
entries.correctiveAction: Small-bucket canonical alpha.25 classes require exactly one scheduling resource.
entries.permanentGuard: Multi-resource scheduling cannot match canonical DLSP/CSLP/PLSP core automatically.

entries.symptom: A test expects ExactCore but its fixture enables an optional problem-class extension, so the analyzer correctly returns CompatibleExtension.
entries.rootCause: Canonical-core fixtures are assembled with convenience defaults that activate unrelated extension semantics.
entries.correctiveAction: Tests asserting ExactCore must explicitly disable every optional extension not listed in the canonical class core.
entries.permanentGuard: DLSP/CSLP ExactCore fixtures must not activate MaximumSetupCount; PLSP retains MaximumSetupCount because the one-transition rule is part of its canonical alpha.25 core.

entries.symptom: A candidate compiles with an xUnit analyzer warning even though the test has an equivalent warning-free assertion API.
entries.rootCause: Test code is validated only for compilation/test success and not for avoidable analyzer warnings.
entries.correctiveAction: Use analyzer-preferred assertion overloads, e.g. Assert.Single(collection, predicate) instead of filtering with Where before Assert.Single.
entries.permanentGuard: New or modified test files must not introduce xUnit analyzer warnings when a canonical warning-free API exists.

entries.symptom: A test expects formulation incompatibility from scheduling extensions even though the scientific classifier has no unique canonical problem class.
entries.rootCause: Extension-level formulation support is evaluated conceptually before the prerequisite problem-class identity is established.
entries.correctiveAction: Preserve the ScientificFormulationCompatibilityService order: without a unique PrimaryProblemClass, return Undetermined (LSDM-FORM-003). Only a uniquely classified unsupported class returns Incompatible (LSDM-FORM-010).
entries.permanentGuard: Checker tests must distinguish classifiable scheduling instances from incomplete scheduling descriptions. Incomplete classification must not be forced to Incompatible by extension flags alone.

entries.symptom: A compatibility test expects KnownUnsupportedExtensions to be populated for a problem class that the formulation profile itself does not support.
entries.rootCause: The test assumes extension analysis continues after canonical problem-class rejection.
entries.correctiveAction: When SupportsProblemClass is false, assert LSDM-FORM-010 and an empty extension-evidence channel; test profile-level unsupported extensions separately.
entries.permanentGuard: Problem-class incompatibility is terminal for one formulation assessment; extension support evidence is only evaluated after the canonical class is supported.
